Bellum Batonianum.fact: In 13 BC, Augustus gave Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, his most important ally, the supreme command in Illyricum.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Command was then given to _____, who finally defeated the Illyrians
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Command was then given to Tiberius, who finally defeated the Illyrians.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Roman military operations in _____ might have started by the time of Marcus Vinicius' governorship in 14–13 BC
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In 13 BC, Augustus gave Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, his most important ally, the supreme command in Illyricum. Roman military operations in Illyricum might have started by the time of Marcus Vinicius' governorship in 14–13 BC.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The Pannonian War led to _____ being redesignated an imperial province
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Roman military operations in Illyricum might have started by the time of Marcus Vinicius' governorship in 14–13 BC. The Pannonian War led to Illyricum being redesignated an imperial province.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The main tribes which contributed to the alliance were the _____, Breuci, Dalmatae, Andizetes, Pannonians, Pirustae, Liburnians, and Iapydes (the latter two fighting under an unknown leader)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The main tribes which contributed to the alliance were the Daesitiatae, Breuci, Dalmatae, Andizetes, Pannonians, Pirustae, Liburnians, and Iapydes (the latter two fighting under an unknown leader).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The Dalmatians were led by Bato the _____, while the Breuci were led by Bato the Breucian, their army commander, and Pinnes, their king
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The Dalmatians were led by Bato the Daesitiate, while the Breuci were led by Bato the Breucian, their army commander, and Pinnes, their king.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The primary sources of this information are _____ and Velleius Paterculus
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The primary sources of this information are Cassius Dio and Velleius Paterculus.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: At one point there were ten legions assembled in _____, but five of them were sent back because this would have created an oversized army
Bellum Batonianum.fact: At one point there were ten legions assembled in Illyricum, but five of them were sent back because this would have created an oversized army. Through most of the war it was the five legions stationed in Illyricum (three in Pannonia and two in Dalmatia) which were engaged in this war, which covered a very large area.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Through most of the war it was the five legions stationed in _____ (three in Pannonia and two in Dalmatia) which were engaged in this war, which covered a very large area
Bellum Batonianum.fact: At one point there were ten legions assembled in Illyricum, but five of them were sent back because this would have created an oversized army. Through most of the war it was the five legions stationed in Illyricum (three in Pannonia and two in Dalmatia) which were engaged in this war, which covered a very large area.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: On three occasions the three legions from the Roman province of _____ were involved in the fighting and on one occasion two legions from the Roman province of Asia were also involved
Bellum Batonianum.fact: On three occasions the three legions from the Roman province of Moesia were involved in the fighting and on one occasion two legions from the Roman province of Asia were also involved.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: In addition, there were irregular emergency units levied in _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In addition, there were irregular emergency units levied in Italy.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The rebels had an efficient military organisation which paralleled that of the _____, given that they had previously served in Roman-trained auxiliary military units
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The rebels had an efficient military organisation which paralleled that of the Romans, given that they had previously served in Roman-trained auxiliary military units.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: There were only three major battles in the area of Sirmium (_____, in modern Serbia), in nearby northern Moesia, and a number of minor battles in Dalmatia
Bellum Batonianum.fact: There were only three major battles in the area of Sirmium (Sremska Mitrovica, in modern Serbia), in nearby northern Moesia, and a number of minor battles in Dalmatia.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Much of the _____ war effort instead involved counter-insurgency operations
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The rebels had an efficient military organisation which paralleled that of the Romans, given that they had previously served in Roman-trained auxiliary military units. Much of the Roman war effort instead involved counter-insurgency operations.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Marcus Valerius Messalla Messallinus, the governor of _____, had planned to join him with most of his army, and ordered the local tribes to provide auxiliary contingents
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Marcus Valerius Messalla Messallinus, the governor of Illyricum, had planned to join him with most of his army, and ordered the local tribes to provide auxiliary contingents.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: However, when these troops gathered, they rebelled under the leadership of a _____ tribal chieftain named Bato and defeated a Roman force sent against them
Bellum Batonianum.fact: However, when these troops gathered, they rebelled under the leadership of a Daesitiate tribal chieftain named Bato and defeated a Roman force sent against them. Although this war is sometimes described as having been fought by the Daesitiatae and the Breuci only, Cassius Dio identified the forces led by Bato the Daesitiate as Dalmatian, indicating a broader composition.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: According to _____, the population of the tribes which rebelled was more than 800,000, and they fielded 200,000 infantry and 9,000 cavalry
Bellum Batonianum.fact: According to Velleius Paterculus, the population of the tribes which rebelled was more than 800,000, and they fielded 200,000 infantry and 9,000 cavalry. Velleius Paterculus also wrote that the rebels knew Roman military tactics and spoke Latin.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Velleius Paterculus also wrote that the rebels knew _____ military tactics and spoke Latin
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus also wrote that the rebels knew Roman military tactics and spoke Latin. One was to invade Italy, which was not far from Nauportus (a Roman fort in present-day Slovenia); one had already entered the Roman province of Macedonia (present-day Greece); and the third fought in their home territories.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: They executed their plan swiftly, massacring _____ civilians and a sizable veteran contingent who were helpless in this remote area
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus also wrote that the rebels knew Roman military tactics and spoke Latin. One was to invade Italy, which was not far from Nauportus (a Roman fort in present-day Slovenia); one had already entered the Roman province of Macedonia (present-day Greece); and the third fought in their home territories.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: They seized and pillaged _____, creating general panic in Rome
Bellum Batonianum.fact: One was to invade Italy, which was not far from Nauportus (a Roman fort in present-day Slovenia); one had already entered the Roman province of Macedonia (present-day Greece); and the third fought in their home territories. They seized and pillaged Macedonia, creating general panic in Rome.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Rich families were ordered to supply freedmen in proportion to their income, which had not been done since the aftermath of the _____ of Cannae two centuries earlier
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Rich families were ordered to supply freedmen in proportion to their income, which had not been done since the aftermath of the Battle of Cannae two centuries earlier.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: He assigned command of the war to _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: He assigned command of the war to Tiberius.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Outposts were placed to prevent them from breaking through to _____, as well as to disrupt their supply lines
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Augustus warned that the rebels could reach Rome in ten days if drastic action was not taken. Outposts were placed to prevent them from breaking through to Rome, as well as to disrupt their supply lines.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: However, once he defeated the _____ force sent against him, more rebels joined him
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The Roman army was organized into several divisions to evade the united forces of the rebels. However, once he defeated the Roman force sent against him, more rebels joined him.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Then the _____, the largest tribe in southern Pannonia, led by a commander also named Bato, marched on Sirmium
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Then the Breuci, the largest tribe in southern Pannonia, led by a commander also named Bato, marched on Sirmium. Hoping to renew the struggle soon because many Romans had fallen, the Breuci called on their allies to join them.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Hoping to renew the struggle soon because many _____ had fallen, the Breuci called on their allies to join them
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Hoping to renew the struggle soon because many Romans had fallen, the Breuci called on their allies to join them. The Drava was to the northwest of Sirmium and the Romans from Moesia must have come from the east or the south.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Cassius Dio did not specify whether _____ broke a siege of the city or prevented the enemy from reaching it
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Aulus Caecina Severus, the governor of the neighbouring province of Moesia (in modern Serbia, south of the River Sava and west of the River Danube) quickly advanced against them and defeated them near the River Dravus (Drava), but suffered many casualties. Cassius Dio did not specify whether Severus broke a siege of the city or prevented the enemy from reaching it.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The Drava was to the northwest of _____ and the Romans from Moesia must have come from the east or the south
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The Drava was to the northwest of Sirmium and the Romans from Moesia must have come from the east or the south. Thus, if Caecina Severus did break a siege of Sirmium, he would have pursued the retreating Breuci until they made a last stand.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Thus, if _____ did break a siege of Sirmium, he would have pursued the retreating Breuci until they made a last stand
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Thus, if Caecina Severus did break a siege of Sirmium, he would have pursued the retreating Breuci until they made a last stand.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The _____ns marched on Salona (in Dalmatia, on the Adriatic coast) but there Bato was defeated and wounded
Bellum Batonianum.fact: The Dalmatians marched on Salona (in Dalmatia, on the Adriatic coast) but there Bato was defeated and wounded.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: He sent other men forward who ravaged the coast down to _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: He sent other men forward who ravaged the coast down to Apollonia.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Tiberius came from _____, fearing an invasion of Italy, and sent Valerius Messallinus ahead
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius came from Germania, fearing an invasion of Italy, and sent Valerius Messallinus ahead.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Even though Bato was not well, he engaged _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius came from Germania, fearing an invasion of Italy, and sent Valerius Messallinus ahead. Even though Bato was not well, he engaged Tiberius.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Velleius Paterculus wrote that Augustus gave the chief command of all Roman forces to _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius came from Germania, fearing an invasion of Italy, and sent Valerius Messallinus ahead. Even though Bato was not well, he engaged Tiberius.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Presumably Valerius Messallinus was then sent to defend _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Presumably Valerius Messallinus was then sent to defend Salona.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: According to _____, Bato the Daesitiate went east to the other Bato and made an alliance with him
Bellum Batonianum.fact: According to Cassius Dio, Bato the Daesitiate went east to the other Bato and made an alliance with him.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: This contrasts with the picture given by _____, in which the rebellion seemed to have a plan and the Dalmatians and the Breuci seemed to have acted in concert from the beginning
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus wrote that Messallinus was surrounded by 20,000 men and had only one legion at only half its normal strength (roughly 2,500 men), yet he routed the enemy and was awarded a triumphal decoration (ornamenta triumphalia) and a place in the procession during Tiberius’ Pannonian triumph. This contrasts with the picture given by Velleius Paterculus, in which the rebellion seemed to have a plan and the Dalmatians and the Breuci seemed to have acted in concert from the beginning.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: They then fought hard against _____, who later went back to Moesia because the Dacians and Sarmatians had crossed the Danube and were ravaging it
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In Dio's account the two Batos occupied Mount Alma (Mount Fruška Gora, Serbia, just north of Sirmium); here they were defeated by the Thracian cavalry of Rhoemetalces (the king of the Odrysian Kingdom in Thrace, an ally of the Romans) which had been sent ahead against them by Caecina Severus, the governor of Moesia. They then fought hard against Severus, who later went back to Moesia because the Dacians and Sarmatians had crossed the Danube and were ravaging it.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Tiberius and _____ lingered in Siscia (Sisak, in present-day central Croatia, the headquarters of the Roman army)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius and Valerius Messallinus lingered in Siscia (Sisak, in present-day central Croatia, the headquarters of the Roman army).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: In the winter the rebels invaded _____ again
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In the winter the rebels invaded Macedonia again. Cassius Dio wrote that they did so again even though he had not mentioned a previous invasion of Macedonia.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Cassius Dio wrote that they did so again even though he had not mentioned a previous invasion of _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In the winter the rebels invaded Macedonia again. Cassius Dio wrote that they did so again even though he had not mentioned a previous invasion of Macedonia.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Modern scholars know about this through the writing of _____ (as noted above)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Modern scholars know about this through the writing of Velleius Paterculus (as noted above).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: They were defeated by _____ and his brother Rhascyporis
Bellum Batonianum.fact: They were defeated by Rhoemetalces and his brother Rhascyporis.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Dio did not mention any action by the _____ there
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Dio did not mention any action by the Romans there.

Bellum Batonianum.fact: However, Tiberius was very active and was conducting a war of attrition and counter-insurgency operations.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Velleius Paterculus wrote that the harsh winter brought rewards because in the following summer all of _____ sought peace
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus wrote that Messallinus was surrounded by 20,000 men and had only one legion at only half its normal strength (roughly 2,500 men), yet he routed the enemy and was awarded a triumphal decoration (ornamenta triumphalia) and a place in the procession during Tiberius’ Pannonian triumph.

Bellum Batonianum.fact: They went to the Claudian Mountains (a mountain range in Pannonia, in Varaždin County in northern Croatia) and took a defensive position in the natural fortifications.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society

Bellum Batonianum.fact: They surrounded the five legions, their auxiliary troops, and the Thracian cavalry and almost inflicted a fatal defeat. The Thracian cavalry was routed and the allied cavalry fled.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: They attacked him unexpectedly when he was encamped near the _____ marshes, but Severus repulsed the attack
Bellum Batonianum.fact: They attacked him unexpectedly when he was encamped near the Volcaean marshes, but Severus repulsed the attack.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Following this battle the _____ army was divided into detachments to overrun as many parts of the country as possible at once
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Following this battle the Roman army was divided into detachments to overrun as many parts of the country as possible at once.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: After the aforementioned battle, _____ and Marcus Plautius Silvanus joined Tiberius and a huge army was assembled
Bellum Batonianum.fact: After the aforementioned battle, Aulus Caecina Severus and Marcus Plautius Silvanus joined Tiberius and a huge army was assembled.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Velleius Paterculus reported that they brought five legions (three from _____ and two from the province of Asia, respectively)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus reported that they brought five legions (three from Moesia and two from the province of Asia, respectively).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Tiberius had five legions (three in _____ and two in Dalmatia)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius had five legions (three in Pannonia and two in Dalmatia).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: The legions were not at full strength as _____ mentioned that there were seventy cohorts (ten legions at full complement would have had 100 cohorts)
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus reported that they brought five legions (three from Moesia and two from the province of Asia, respectively). The legions were not at full strength as Velleius Paterculus mentioned that there were seventy cohorts (ten legions at full complement would have had 100 cohorts).

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: There were fourteen troops of cavalry, as well as 10,000 reservists, many volunteers, and the _____ cavalry
Bellum Batonianum.fact: There were fourteen troops of cavalry, as well as 10,000 reservists, many volunteers, and the Thracian cavalry.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: There had not been such a large army gathered in a single location since the time of the _____ civil wars
Bellum Batonianum.fact: There had not been such a large army gathered in a single location since the time of the Roman civil wars.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Cassius Dio also noted that there were grain shortages in _____ the previous year and that later in this year the famine abated
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Cassius Dio also noted that there were grain shortages in Rome the previous year and that later in this year the famine abated.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: It is not known how widespread this famine was and whether it touched other _____ areas, including Dalmatia and Pannonia, and thus had been a contributory factor
Bellum Batonianum.fact: It is not known how widespread this famine was and whether it touched other Mediterranean areas, including Dalmatia and Pannonia, and thus had been a contributory factor.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: According to Dio, Bato the _____ overthrew Pinnes, the king of the Breuci
Bellum Batonianum.fact: According to Dio, Bato the Breucian overthrew Pinnes, the king of the Breuci.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: He was handed over to Bato the _____ and was executed
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Bato the Daesitiate defeated him in battle and pinned him in a stronghold. He was handed over to Bato the Daesitiate and was executed.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: After this many _____ broke with the rebels
Bellum Batonianum.fact: After this many Pannonians broke with the rebels.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Marcus Plautius Silvanus conducted a campaign against the tribes, conquered the _____, and won over the others without a battle

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Bato the _____ subsequently withdrew from Pannonia, occupied the passes leading to Dalmatia, and ravaged the lands beyond
Bellum Batonianum.fact: He was handed over to Bato the Daesitiate and was executed. Bato the Daesitiate subsequently withdrew from Pannonia, occupied the passes leading to Dalmatia, and ravaged the lands beyond.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Bato was captured and _____ surrendered
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Bato was captured and Pinnes surrendered.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: In the summer, _____ made his way to Tiberius through areas which had not been affected by the war, and was attacked by fresh local forces
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Velleius Paterculus wrote that Augustus gave the chief command of all Roman forces to Marcus Aemilius Lepidus. In the summer, Lepidus made his way to Tiberius through areas which had not been affected by the war, and was attacked by fresh local forces.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Lepidus defeated them, ravaged the fields, and burnt houses, later reaching _____
Bellum Batonianum.fact: In the summer, Lepidus made his way to Tiberius through areas which had not been affected by the war, and was attacked by fresh local forces. Lepidus defeated them, ravaged the fields, and burnt houses, later reaching Tiberius.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Germanicus was unable to take the well-fortified _____ by storm
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Germanicus was unable to take the well-fortified Splonum by storm.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: When the _____ entered the town they did not notice it and then found themselves surrounded by the flames and pelted from the wall of the citadel, most of them dying in the trap
Bellum Batonianum.fact: When the Romans entered the town they did not notice it and then found themselves surrounded by the flames and pelted from the wall of the citadel, most of them dying in the trap.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Germanicus then seized _____ and then the other places fell easily
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Germanicus then seized Seretium and then the other places fell easily.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: However, other _____ revolted
Bellum Batonianum.fact: However, other Dalmatians revolted.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Cassius Dio also wrote that there was famine in _____ largely due to the war

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society

Bellum Batonianum.fact: However, most of the grain was imported from Egypt, the province of Africa, Sicily, and Sardinia.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Therefore, it is unclear how the war in _____ caused famine in Italy
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Therefore, it is unclear how the war in Illyricum caused famine in Italy.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Augustus sent _____ back to Dalmatia
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Augustus sent Tiberius back to Dalmatia. Tiberius split the army into three divisions to avoid a mutiny.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: He put _____ and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus in charge of two of them and led the third against Bato, taking Germanicus with him

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Tiberius chased the fugitive Bato around the country, and finally besieged him at _____, near Salona

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Tiberius held on until _____ was forced to seek terms
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Tiberius chased the fugitive Bato around the country, and finally besieged him at Adetrium, near Salona. Tiberius held on until Bato was forced to seek terms.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: On seeing this, the _____ lined up outside the wall at the top of the slope and hurled stones at them, separating the Romans further
Bellum Batonianum.fact: On seeing this, the Dalmatians lined up outside the wall at the top of the slope and hurled stones at them, separating the Romans further.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Germanicus turned his attention to the last holdouts in _____, a strongly fortified town with a river around its base
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Germanicus turned his attention to the last holdouts in Arduba, a strongly fortified town with a river around its base.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: Germanicus rejoined _____, and sent Gaius Vibius Postumus to subdue the other districts
Bellum Batonianum.fact: Germanicus rejoined Tiberius, and sent Gaius Vibius Postumus to subdue the other districts. Tiberius agreed and then asked him why his people had rebelled.

Bellum Batonianum.subject: Women & Society
Bellum Batonianum.question: During the war, split _____ tribes into different groups from the ones they had previously composed
Bellum Batonianum.fact: During the war, split Illyrian tribes into different groups from the ones they had previously composed.

Capture of Valkenburg (1574).question: For the cowardice demonstrated at Valkenburg, the _____ troops were rejected by the Dutch rebel army at Leiden, and finally Chester's troops surrendered to the Spanish army
Capture of Valkenburg (1574).fact: The fortress of Valkenburg (northwest of Leiden), garrisoned by five companies of English volunteers commanded by Colonel Edward Chester, was of strategic importance to facilitate (or complicate) the Spanish efforts at Leiden.
